[short] skip

# Test file
! go test p1_test.go
stderr 'Logf format %d'
go test -vet=off
stdout '^ok'

# Non-test file
! go test p1.go
stderr 'Printf format %d'
go test -x -vet=shift p1.go
stderr '[\\/]vet.*-shift'
stdout '\[no test files\]'
go test -vet=off p1.go
! stderr '[\\/]vet.*-shift'
stdout '\[no test files\]'

# Test issue #22890
go test m/vetcycle
stdout 'm/vetcycle.*\[no test files\]'

# Test with ...
! go test ./vetfail/...
stderr 'Printf format %d'
stdout 'ok\s+m/vetfail/p2'

# Check there's no diagnosis of a bad build constraint in vetxonly mode.
# Use -a so that we need to recompute the vet-specific export data for
# vetfail/p1.
go test -a m/vetfail/p2
! stderr 'invalid.*constraint'

# An invalid //go:debug directive is reported only once when build and vet
# run concurrently during 'go test'.
! go test m/baddebug
stderr -count=1 'invalid //go:debug'

# If the vet tool fails without producing vet.out while the build succeeds,
# both 'go test' and 'go test -c' must report the error and fail.
go build -o $WORK/failvet$GOEXE ./failvet
! go test -toolexec=$WORK/failvet$GOEXE m/okpkg
stderr 'vet tool crashed'
stdout 'FAIL\tm/okpkg \[build failed\]'
! go test -c -toolexec=$WORK/failvet$GOEXE m/okpkg
stderr 'vet tool crashed'
! exists okpkg.test$GOEXE
! go test -c -o $devnull -toolexec=$WORK/failvet$GOEXE m/okpkg
stderr 'vet tool crashed'

-- failvet/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

func main() {
	tool := strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(os.Args[1]), ".exe")
	if tool == "vet" && (len(os.Args) < 3 || os.Args[2] != "-V=full") {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "vet tool crashed")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	cmd := exec.Command(os.Args[1], os.Args[2:]...)
	cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		if ee, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
			os.Exit(ee.ExitCode())
		}
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
